title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Evan Kim
description: Motivation: reduce unit token cost and variance for hosted and dedicated customers by providing safe default autotune profiles for batching/caching and quantization. This PR implements: 1) conservative default batching and prefix/KV caching parameters that are safe for low-latency SLOs but increase throughput for bursty workloads; 2) a set of validated quantization profiles (8-bit, mixed-8/4) with heuristics to select a profile by model family and request distribution; 3) new unit-economics instrumentation and tooling surfaced in Redwood Console and rwdctl so teams can measure per-route token cost breakdowns and simulated savings from autotune suggestions; 4) an autoscaler hook to prefer cost-optimized variants during low utilization windows. Summary of changes in this single PR: - runtime: add autotune defaults and profile selection logic - serving: integrate quant profiles into model variant registry - optimize: CLI and console changes to preview unit-econ impact - tests: new integration tests that validate latency/regression thresholds - docs: guidance and migration notes Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-4321) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks for 3 models (redwood-7b, redwood-14b, llama-2-13b) - [x] Console UI mock + UX review - [x] Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-in for Dedicated customers via policy - [x] Release notes included Notes: In benchmarks across representative workloads we saw ~9-15% lower token cost with <5% latency regression at p50 and controlled p95 impact when using autotuned batching+caching and quant profiles. The PR keeps conservative fallbacks to full-precision variants if quality regressions exceed configured thresholds. Related: ENG-4200 (kv-cache improvements), ENG-3981 (quant kernels).

Evan Kim (author): We made hosted default conservative (fp16 preferred) and added a gate in the console to opt into aggressive quant tiers per model. See autosave flag in console UI and model-registry/quant_profiles.yaml
Marco Rossi (reviewer): Scheduler hook looks good but can we add a fallback policy that forces full-precision if eval regressions are detected?
Evan Kim (author): Added a regression detector and policy that flips variants back to the last-known-good version and posts an alert. See serving/runtime/autotune.py lines (added).
Dana Liu (reviewer): Unit-econ preview endpoint should rate-limit expensive simulations. Suggest caching results for 10 minutes per route.
Evan Kim (author): Added caching layer in unit_econ_service.go and a default TTL of 10m.
